_note: The product's vocabulary, split by who reads it. Kettle keeps precise internal terms AND talks to users about their project in words they already have; this file is where those two stay straight. `tools/lint-lexicon.py` fails CI on a house word reaching the screen, and on spelling drift in the prompt corpus. Projected to docs/LEXICON.md; rendered into the agent handbook.

_casing.title: A proper name — a document, or a named control that is also a title. Always exactly as `term`, mid-sentence included. docs/UI.md: signature actions that are also titles stay Title Case.
_casing.lower: A common noun or verb. Lowercase in prose; a capital is correct only at the start of a sentence or inside a Title Case heading. `sweep` the act is lowercase; `Sweep` the control is its own entry.

terms.gloss: One project as Kettle holds it: its notes, memory, queue and records, in the project's desk directory. House word. On screen a user has a **project** — never a desk, and never a "project desk": a user should not have to learn what a desk is to use Kettle.
One working session at a desk: the user reviews the queue, rules on entries, and closes with a sweep. The web UI as a whole is 'the sitting'.

not_synonyms.why: 'session' is the `curator`'s conversation state, not the user's working period

terms.gloss: The batch of entries the curator has staged for this sitting, ranked by urgency.

not_synonyms.why: the inbox kit is a specific kit; the queue is the general structure
entries are files to read, not tasks

terms.gloss: One item in the queue: a file, plus its ask, brief, urgency, and status. 'queue entry' in full where the context needs it.

not_synonyms.why: not an issue tracker
not a board

terms.gloss: The curator's 2-4 sentence introduction to an entry, shown the instant the file loads. A clear, unassuming introduction, not a dense memo. Standard: kits/frameworks/brief.md.

not_synonyms.why: a brief introduces and orients; it does not summarise the file
vague where the standard is specific

terms.gloss: The one-line question an entry puts to the user — what judgment is wanted on this file.

not_synonyms.why: the product word is ask
'prompt' means the `curator`'s instructions

terms.lint_note: Not checked on screen: the house term is the noun (an entry's one-line question), and `ask` is also an ordinary verb a user reads without trouble. A regex cannot tell them apart, and flagging 'Ask the agent' is the kind of noise that gets a linter switched off.

terms.gloss: The user's judgment on an entry, bookmarked by Approve. A ruling is not applied until the sitting is swept.

not_synonyms.why: reserve 'decision' for design decisions in docs
not the product word

terms.gloss: Finishing a batch: apply the user's decisions, review what changed, note the ripples, save a record, line up the next files. The one invented word Kettle asks a user to learn, and only because it is a button they press — so prose says what it does ('press Sweep: the agent applies your decisions') rather than assuming they know.

not_synonyms.why: a sweep is not a synchronisation
a sweep does not make a git commit

terms.gloss: The project's resident agent: curates the queue, converses about the open file, and sweeps. Its identity lives in files, not in a session, so any model that reads them is the agent. Renamed from `curator` on 2026-10-01; the verb `curate` and the adjective `curatorial` survive, and so does every identifier (`curator.provider` in settings, `/api/curator`, `curatorProvider`), which is contract, not copy.

not_synonyms.why: generic; the agent is a defined role
never refer to the agent this way in product copy
never refer to the agent this way in product copy

retired.why: the role is `agent` in user-facing copy (2026-10-01)
the role is `agent` in user-facing copy (2026-10-01)

terms.gloss: What a desk is for and how it should be worked, written at founding. Lives in PROJECT.md. A desk is founded only when a charter exists and the queue holds at least one content entry.

not_synonyms.why: a charter is prose the user and `curator` both read

terms.gloss: The desk's distilled standing knowledge, in MEMORY.md. Memory is distillation — it is never a transcript.
A signal staged in the desk's outbound/ folder for another agent or system. Staged, never transmitted from the curator sandbox.

not_synonyms.why: the inbox kit's <root>/outbox is a different thing: approved mail drafts

terms.gloss: Bringing a desk into being: register, survey, interview, Draft Proposal, `Found Desk`. Founding is a conversation, not a confirmation card.

not_synonyms.why: not the product word
founding is a conversation; a wizard is the thing it is not

terms.gloss: The tool-less conversation in which the curator learns what the project is and what the user wants from a second reader. A common noun: lowercase in prose. Lowercase in prose; as a pane hed it takes Title Case like any hed (docs/UI.md), which is why `Founding Interview` is correct in the status strip.

not_synonyms.why: see founding

terms.gloss: The document the setup questions produce, written to DESK-PROPOSAL.md. House name. On screen it is just **the proposal**.

not_synonyms.why: not a product term
not a product term

terms.gloss: The control that ends the founding interview early and writes the Desk Proposal. Carries a check glyph in the sitting: 'Draft Proposal ✓'.
The control that registers a project and opens founding. docs/UI.md lists it among the signature actions that are also titles.

The control that rules on the open entry. On a founded project desk it bookmarks a ruling and applies nothing until a sweep. While a proposal is open it founds the project desk — the label no longer changes, so the sitting promotes the control visually instead (`body.proposing #approve`).

not_synonyms.why: not the product word

terms.lint_note: Not case-checked: the term is a single ordinary word, so a lowercase occurrence is the concept, not a misspelling of the control.

retired.why: the control reads Approve in both states (2026-10-01); `found` survives as the verb

terms.gloss: The control that closes the sitting. The act is 'sweep' (lowercase); this entry is the named control only.
terms.lint_note: Not case-checked: the term is a single ordinary word, so a lowercase occurrence is the concept, not a misspelling of the control.

terms.gloss: The control that opens a note on the open file for the curator to address during the sweep.
terms.lint_note: Not case-checked: the term is a single ordinary word, so a lowercase occurrence is the concept, not a misspelling of the control.

terms.gloss: A client onto a desk: the web sitting, the desktop shell, the TUI, the VS Code Desk, the CLI. Every viewport attaches to the same desk and the same API.

not_synonyms.why: there are several, and they are not all web
not the product word

terms.gloss: The panel kettle-vscode contributes to VS Code and Cursor. Name it in full. A bare `Desk` for the panel collides with `desk` the common noun and reads as a stray capital; write `the Desk panel` only where the context is already VS Code.

not_synonyms.why: the extension is the package; the panel it contributes is the `VS Code Desk`

_fields.avoid: Literal wrong spellings of THIS term. Decidable by a linter, so these are errors.
_fields.not_synonyms: Different words that do not mean this term. Guidance for writers and for the curator; never linted, because only a reader can tell whether 'summary' is standing in for 'brief'.
_fields.lint_case: false when the term is a single ordinary word and the lowercase form is legitimately the concept.
_fields.retired: Literal strings that used to mean this term and must not come back (an old button label, a renamed document). Decidable, so these are errors too.
_fields.plain: For a `house` term: what a user sees instead. The linter quotes it as the fix.
_fields.lint_house: false when the house word is also an ordinary English word in another part of speech, so the on-screen check would fire on correct copy.

_audience.house: Code, prompts, docs, and our own conversation. Precision for us. A `house` term appearing in ui-copy.json is an error: see `plain` for what the user reads instead.
_audience.both: Plain enough that a user reads it without being taught, or a control label they learn by pressing. Allowed everywhere.
